summary: Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Yangon (~1927–1935), under Pe Maung Tin (~1931–1935), and at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee, an Indologist, completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar and held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Mineo Hashimoto (1924–1984) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1949) and served at Kobe University from around 1960 to 1984.

Buddhist studies scholar Ming Mei earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan. Ming Mei also studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. After earning a BA at the University of Hong Kong and a PhD at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, Liu became a professor at HKU around 1979.
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

Minori Nishimura (b. 1947), a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD at Taisho University (~1970–1976), where Nishimura taught (~1993–2018). Nishimura also held researcher roles at Sanko Research Institute and Eastern Institute.

Indologist Minoru Hara (1930–2021) studied at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and Cambridge. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1975–1991), president of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and director of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees after studying at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa. He was a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1966 to 1994.

Linguist Minton Warren (1850–1907) studied at Tufts, Yale, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). He taught Latin at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899) and Harvard (from 1899), and headed the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899).
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mio Shinma (b. 1949) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies, serving as a professor (attested 2007) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Hanazono University.
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Mipam Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. As a teacher, his students included Shenphen Nangwa, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Terton Sogyal.

Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies under Masatoshi Nagatomi, was taught by Robert A. F. Thurman, and had Bratindra Nath Mukherjee as a postdoctoral mentor.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Universities of Bucharest and Calcutta, and held posts at Bucharest, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Chicago.
Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology and held posts at the National Centre for Scientific Research as Chargé de Recherche and at Paris Nanterre University (both attested 1985).

Mirella Lingorska specializes in Indology and linguistics. She has held posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).
